newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on Sparks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on Sparks estimate.

text.p: Bullish input from reports Sparks Companies estimated the 1996 U.S. soybean crop at 2.367 billion bushels boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"We followed Sparks. He set the tone and that's the tune we danced to," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Traders said the market had been braced for a soybean production tally of nearer 2.4 billion bushels. USDA's October forecast pegged the U.S. soybean crop at 2.346 billion bushels and a new government forecast is slated for release Tuesday.
The Leslie-ADM Elevator Survey will be released Friday.
Support also came from strong stopping of the deliveries posted Wednesday against the November contract, the traders said.
The ADM Investor Services house account stopped 1.735 million of the 2.115 million bushels posted Wednesday for delivery on the November, the CBOT said.
Traders also said the market was oversold with the daily nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November moving between 30 and 40 points. Thirty is considered oversold.
Soybeans closed six to 11 cents per bushel higher, with November up 11 at $6.81.
The nearby November contract again started to bubble on spreads relative to other months with the presence of a valid commercial stopper Wednesday foremost in traders minds.
"ADM stopping beans helped the spreads plus they're talking about a crush of over 30 million bushels tomorrow which would be a record," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The National Oilseeds Processors Association late Thursday will release its updated weekly soybean crush report. Also, early Thursday USDA will reveal its weekly soy export report.
"They're talking about a bean sales number of 500,000 to 750,000 tonnes," Kucha said of projected soy exports.
There was scattered commission house and fund buying of soybean futures Wednesday with the key volume player being E.D. and F. Man's sale of four million bushels of January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000, down from 52,702 Tuesday.
In soybean options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 1,000 January $7.25 calls at 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 16,000, up from 15,390 Tuesday.
